what_it_says: Tertullian says the Word, which God made all things by, is proceeded forth from God and generated by that procession, and so called Son of God and God from the unity of substance.

page: printed p. 64 of the ANF vol. 3 scan (PDF p. 62)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 3 (A. Cleveland Coxe, American reprint), Buffalo: The Christian Literature Co., 1885-1896 (scan title page; pagination runs continuously through the scan)
what_it_says: Tertullian says the Son is "God of God" and "Spirit of Spirit", made a second in manner of existence (in position, not in nature), and did not withdraw from the source but went forth.
use: Key text for the divinity of the Son: "second" is in position (gradus) and not in nature (status); the Son is one God with the Father in substance.
limits: "Second" (numerum gradu, non statu) is the phrase opponents quote. The Latin here is from the Latin Library only; the Latin edition of Apologeticum 21 was not compared to a scan (Souter 1917 not located on archive.org in this session).

english: Not that in the waters we obtain the Holy Spirit; but in the water, under (the witness of) the angel, we are cleansed, and prepared for the Holy Spirit. In this case also a type has preceded; for thus was John beforehand the Lord’s forerunner, “preparing His ways.” Thus, too, does the angel, the witness of baptism, “make the paths straight” for the Holy Spirit, who is about to come upon us, by the washing away of sins, which faith, sealed in (the name of) the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, obtains.
page: printed p. 1260 of the ANF vol. 3 scan (PDF p. 1258)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 3 (A. Cleveland Coxe, American reprint), Buffalo: The Christian Literature Co., 1885-1896 (scan title page; pagination runs continuously through the scan)
what_it_says: Tertullian says faith is sealed "in the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit" in baptism, and that the three are witnesses of our faith.
use: Baptismal formula as early witness to the three-fold name of God as one object of faith (names of Father, Son, Holy Spirit, one name).
limits: The formula is a witness to the naming, not a definition of consubstantiality. The Latin of ch. 6.2 ("ubi tres, id est pater et filius et spiritus sanctus") is not quoted here.
